CLINICAL DOCUMENTATION — NARRATIVE EMERGENCY OBSERVATION NOTE V1
Patient: Elizabeth Rodriguez | MRN: PAT-60010 | DOB: 1978-10-25 | Gender: Female | Doc ID: NARRATIVE_0010
Encounter Date: 2025-04-14 | Discharge/Note Date: 2025-04-19 | Provider: Dr. Sarah Jenkins, MD
EMERGENCY DEPARTMENT PRESENTATION
Patient Elizabeth Rodriguez was triaged in the emergency department following acute onset of lightheadedness and
palpitations earlier this morning. Initial hemodynamic parameters were reviewed and patient was placed on telemetry.
HISTORY OF PRESENT ILLNESS
The patient describes experiencing recurrent lightheadedness over the preceding 48 hours without syncope. Initial
emergency workup revealed that initial platelet count was measured at 245 10*3/uL. Point-of-care laboratory screening
additionally noted white blood cell count resulted at 14.7 10*3/uL (HIGH). Given these findings, the patient was transitioned
to the Clinical Decision Unit for 24-hour observation.
OBSERVATION UNIT CLINICAL COURSE
Throughout the observation unit stay, continuous telemetry showed normal sinus rhythm without pause or tachyarrhythmia.
The patient was administered Amlodipine at a dose of 2.5 mg orally once daily, which promptly alleviated acute symptoms.
Follow-up protocol monitoring of calcium demonstrated 7.65 mg/dL (LOW). Orthostatic blood pressures were negative upon
ambulation.
DISCHARGE REGIMEN
Patient was deemed safe for outpatient discharge. The ongoing regimen includes Omeprazole 40 mg PO once daily in the
morning for 14 days as prescribed. Prescription counseling was performed by nursing prior to release.
PLAN & PRECAUTIONS
Resume normal daily activities as tolerated. Avoid strenuous exercise until cardiology follow-up in 1 to 2 weeks. Immediate
emergency precautions detailed.
